design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (non-workflow task, difficulty savings_withdrawals_interest_and_transfers, M=2, final task). Current as of round 8; the revision log at the end records how it got here.

[Scope snapshot] Occupied by task 0: savings_ext_certificate_proceeds_transfer, savings_ext_same_contact_reactivation, savings_ext_best_money_market_conversion, the single workflow savings_wf_dormant_account_wakeup_and_upgrade, and tools transfer_savings_to_checking_5f60835b, reactivate_savings_account_bfe70db1, refund_savings_maintenance_fee_bf99bb2f, convert_savings_tier_d500151b. Claimed here (disjoint): savings_ext_certificate_funding_fee_refund, savings_ext_counted_withdrawal_fee_assessment, savings_ext_overdraft_replenishment_transfer; tools refund_savings_withdrawal_fee_774e6cc0, assess_savings_withdrawal_fee_aafc1fb2, set_savings_automatic_transfer_e1e909eb; workflows []. The two tasks together cover all six extended policies, each claimed once.

[Why this is a good test] Rochelle Gaither asks for one thing: a monthly automatic transfer that "puts back what overdraft protection pulled out of my savings this statement period, plus whatever withdrawal fees the savings actually ends up paying for this period". The amount depends on the withdrawal fees the account really bears for the current cycle 2026-09, and two hidden problems make the opening ledger wrong. First, a 15.00 excess withdrawal fee (more than even the Statement Savings fee of 10.00) was charged on the 5,000.00 internal transfer that funded her 6-Month Certificate; internal_transfer never counts, so the whole fee is a bank error. Second, the seventh counted withdrawal, the 47.80 overdraft transfer of 2026-09-09, carries no fee although the allowance is 6. The agent must take the cycle from the most recent overdraft protection transfer (its counterparty is her own checking account, and the cycle is the current one), count counted channels in posting order (online 08-21, overdraft 08-24, 08-27, 08-31, 09-03, telephone 09-08, overdraft 09-09; the ATM withdrawal of 08-25 and the internal transfer of 08-28 excluded), refund the erroneous fee first (a fee refunded as bank_error covers no withdrawal, while it still counts toward the per-cycle maximum), then charge the owed fee, then compute 527.55 + (25.00 - 15.00) = 537.55. Every shortcut gives a different number: the opening ledger (neither prerequisite) gives 542.55, refunding without assessing gives 527.55, assessing without refunding gives 552.55, and reconciling before the refund charges nothing and leaves 542.55.

[Problem-tree card] root_problem = savings_ext_overdraft_replenishment_transfer (action 11). Edge (1): root -> savings_ext_counted_withdrawal_fee_assessment, value_input, gate fees_net, condition "Every excess withdrawal fee owed for the cycle has been charged before the monthly replenishment amount is computed.", policy_source "The fees the account bears are counted only after every excess withdrawal fee refund and every excess withdrawal fee owed for the cycle has been posted.", resolved_by assess_savings_withdrawal_fee_aafc1fb2; false at frozen_time because initial_state.savings_transactions.<od5> (overdraft_transfer, 2026-09-09, cycle 2026-09) has no fee pointing at it. Edge (2): root -> savings_ext_certificate_funding_fee_refund, value_input, gate fees_net, condition "Every excess withdrawal fee refund owed for the cycle has been posted before the monthly replenishment amount is computed.", the same policy_source, resolved_by refund_savings_withdrawal_fee_774e6cc0; false because initial_state.savings_transactions.<fee_cd> (excess_withdrawal 15.00, source = the internal transfer <w_cd>) has no refund row. Edge (3): assessment -> refund, value_input, gate voided, condition "Every excess withdrawal fee of the cycle assessed contrary to the charter has been refunded before the fees owed are counted.", policy_source "Before the fees owed are counted, every excess withdrawal fee of the cycle that was assessed contrary to the charter must already have been refunded." Shape: a chain (root -> assessment -> refund) plus a parallel edge (root -> refund). Topological order refund (7) -> assessment (9) -> transfer (11), pinned by the policy text. Deletion sensitivity (check_compute replay plus hand replay): without step 9 the amount is 527.55; without step 7 (step 9 kept) it is 552.55; without both it is 542.55; without step 7 the assessment computes 0.00 instead of 10.00. user_scenario names none of the fees, refunds or counts, and no tool validates anything.

[Base-invariant card] Action 7 (savings_fee_refund), savings_evt_fee_refund: eligible_fee_code (excess_withdrawal is courtesy-eligible), courtesy_window (anchor savings_transactions.posted_date 2026-08-28, 60 calendar days counted from the next day, inclusive, last day 2026-10-27; frozen 2026-09-10 = day 13), courtesy_limit (no savings courtesy refund in 365 days; limit 1), account_open (active), refund_once (no refund points at the fee). Action 9 (savings_fee): every base eligibility gate whose applies_to names savings_fee is registered, whether or not it concerns an excess withdrawal fee: maintenance.active_at_close (status active), maintenance.one_per_cycle (no maintenance fee in 2026-09, bound to the account and cycle 2026-09), withdrawal_allowance.one_fee_per_withdrawal (no fee yet on the 09-09 transfer), dormancy (scope only: active account, activity 2026-09-08) and closure.early_window. early_window governs only the early closure fee ("The early closure fee applies when the account is closed within early_closure_window_days calendar days after the account was opened"); it is registered because its applies_to lists savings_fee, its own arithmetic holds at frozen_time (opened 2026-06-24, last day 2026-09-22), and it neither permits nor bars an excess withdrawal fee at any date. Base per-cycle maximum: savings_msr_cycle_excess_fees counts every excess fee row posted in 2026-09 (one, the erroneous fee), so 5 more may be charged; the assessment follows exactly that count. Action 11 (savings_set_automatic_transfer): funding_account_owned_active (checking 2605 belongs to the same customer, status active), minimum_amount (537.55 >= 25.00).

[Business-object card] Account: Statement Savings ending 3318 (her only savings account). Cycle reconciled and replenished: 2026-09 (cycle day 20, 2026-08-21..2026-09-20), the statement_cycle of the most recent overdraft protection transfer (2026-09-09), whose counterparty is her own checking account 2605, and the current cycle at frozen_time. Overdraft transfers entering the total: 5 rows (120.00, 85.50, 64.25, 210.00, 47.80); excluded: the online 400.00 of 2026-08-11 (cycle 2026-08), the online 300.00 and telephone 150.00 (counted, but not overdraft pulls), the ATM 60.00 and the 5,000.00 certificate funding. Fees: the erroneous 15.00 (source = the certificate funding transfer) is refunded by a bank_error row posted in 2026-09 whose source_item_id is that fee, a fee of the same cycle; the new 10.00 fee's source_item_id is the 09-09 overdraft transfer.

[World rows] customers (identity); checking_accounts Everyday Checking ending 2605 with overdraft_link_savings_account_id = this savings (the counterparty of every overdraft transfer, and the funding account); cd_certificates 6-Month Certificate opened 2026-08-28, active, 5,000.00 (the counterparty of the latest internal-transfer withdrawal); savings_accounts row (tier, cycle day 20, opened 2026-06-24); 18 ledger rows: opening branch 6,000.00, mobile 850.00, ACH payroll 1,200.00, online 400.00 (cycle 2026-08), four interest credits (base and relationship bonus 0.24/0.24 for 2026-07 and 0.32/0.32 for 2026-08, computed day by day at 0.05 APY plus the 0.05 bonus for an Everyday Checking holder), and the ten cycle-2026-09 rows above. Balance 1,598.57 equals the ledger sum and covered every withdrawal when it posted. Automatic clauses checked: no maintenance fee for the opening cycle 2026-07, 2026-08 waived by the minimum daily balance (never below 300), cycle 2026-09 not yet closed, no automatic transfer yet, no dormancy.

[Persona design] Rochelle Gaither, 36, dental hygienist on a break: friendly, rushed, trusts the agent with arithmetic. Volunteered: the goal sentence and the 22nd (her pay lands the day before). On request: mobile 8645550126, DOB 1989-10-03, SSN 3147, ZIP 29607 (email only as a fallback), savings ending 3318, Everyday checking ending 2605 as the source. Passive reactions: pleased if told a fee is being returned; sighs but accepts if told an owed fee is being added, and asks that the monthly amount still cover everything; keeps overdraft protection unchanged; declines politely any courtesy or favor waiver of a fee ("you only want what the bank's own rules say, nothing extra"), so no courtesy_waiver row can arise; runs the handed-over tool with the amount, day and accounts the agent reads out; does not question the agent's arithmetic and has no recheck branch; hangs up once the transfer is confirmed. She never names a figure, fee or step.

[Local closure (non-workflow)] savings_ext_certificate_funding_fee_refund -> refund_savings_withdrawal_fee_774e6cc0 -> computation step 7 amount 15.00; savings_ext_counted_withdrawal_fee_assessment -> assess_savings_withdrawal_fee_aafc1fb2 -> step 9 amount 10.00; savings_ext_overdraft_replenishment_transfer -> set_savings_automatic_transfer_e1e909eb -> step 11 automatic_transfer_amount 537.55. charter_scope.extended_policies = the computations' policy set = required_documents (same order); task_tools in first-call order; workflows []. Each action is a synchronous posting or instruction at frozen_time 2026-09-10 09:40 EDT; nothing waits for the first transfer run.

[Rule <-> compute sweep] Refund: latest internal-transfer withdrawal date -> d_out; "exactly one internal-transfer withdrawal posted on that most recent date" -> n_out; its counterparty -> fund_cp; "taken only when its counterparty is a certificate of deposit held by the same customer" -> cd_id = CFIELD('cd','certificate_id', certificate_id=fund_cp), an exact-id read; the transfer itself -> fund_wd; counted-channel exclusion -> counted_flag (untriggered); the fee on that transfer at its full posted amount -> fee_amt, result. Assessment: most recent overdraft protection transfer date -> od_d; its counterparty -> od_cp; "When overdraft protection transfers to different accounts posted on that most recent date ... nothing is reconciled" -> od_same (so no row order is used); "taken only when its counterparty is a checking account of the same customer" -> od_chk (exact-id read); its statement_cycle -> cyc; channel-by-channel counting with the tier list -> n_online..n_wire (money_market_check untriggered for Statement Savings); every overdraft transfer of the cycle when the tier flag is true -> n_od; withdrawals beyond the allowance, unlimited branch -> free, beyond; every fee row of the cycle -> fee_rows (the rows savings_msr_cycle_excess_fees counts, given the condition that the fee rows posted within the cycle's dates are exactly those belonging to it); bank_error refunds posted in the cycle -> voided; fees that cover a withdrawal -> covered = fee_rows - voided; the room left under the maximum, counting every row -> room; owed = MN(beyond - covered, room) floored at none; fee amount -> result. The rules state their applicability conditions explicitly as conditions the computed value does not test, each readable from the records: for the assessment, the cycle is the current statement cycle (frozen date and statement_cycle_day), the frozen date is a business day so that the refund made in the contact and the new fee post on it (2026-09-10 is a Thursday and no Federal Reserve holiday), every excess fee row posted within the cycle's dates belongs to the cycle and every one belonging to it posted within them (posted_date and statement_cycle; here the one fee row posted 2026-08-28, inside 2026-08-21..2026-09-20), every unrefunded excess fee of the cycle sits on a counted withdrawal beyond the allowance and every bank_error-refunded one sits on another withdrawal (source_item_id), every bank_error excess-fee refund posted in the cycle refunds a fee of that cycle and every bank_error refund of a fee of the cycle posted in the cycle (source_item_id and statement_cycle), and no two counted withdrawals of the cycle posted on the same day (posted dates; here the seven counted withdrawals fall on seven different days, 08-21, 08-24, 08-27, 08-31, 09-03, 09-08 and 09-09); for the replenishment, the current-cycle condition, the condition that no row on the account has a posted_date later than the frozen date (here the latest is 2026-09-10, the day the refund and the fee posted), and the same-cycle-refund condition. No compute_basis entry attributes these conditions to a binding. Replenishment: od_d, od_cp, od_same, od_chk, cyc as above ("no amount is computed under this policy" when od_chk is null -> result 0); every overdraft transfer of the cycle -> od_total; "the withdrawal fees the account bears" = fee amounts less every refund amount posted in the cycle, zero floor -> fees, refunds, fees_net; the minimum raise and rounding -> floor, result (the raise is untriggered). Every compute_basis quotation is a verbatim substring of its rule (checked mechanically).

[Standard solution and verification] find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, DOB, SSN4, ZIP) -> find_savings_accounts -> find_savings_transactions -> find_checking_accounts -> find_cd_certificates -> refund fee_cd 15.00 bank_error cycle 2026-09 -> assess 10.00 on the 09-09 overdraft transfer, cycle 2026-09 -> hand over the automatic transfer tool; she sets 537.55 on day 22 from checking 2605. Gates run (round 5): EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK (closure 22/22, deterministic, no errors), SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK (handling-time recompute equals expected and gold; value_input replays give assessment 0.00 without the refund, amount 527.55 without the assessment and 552.55 without the refund), GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK.

[solvability_contract vs GT] The refund bindings resolve to the fee id and the customer id that are passed. The assessment bindings resolve account 3318, cycle 2026-09 and the 09-09 withdrawal id passed as source_item_id. Both time gates (courtesy_window at 7, early_window at 9) deep-copy the base temporal_basis, with boundary days 2026-10-27/28 and 2026-09-22/23; the early_window entry records the window's own arithmetic only. The automatic-transfer gates bind checking 2605 and account 3318.

[Draft recomputation from visible context] From the published rules only: the replenishment rule says the fees the account bears are counted only after every refund and every owed fee has posted -> look at the excess fees of the current cycle 2026-09 -> the only one sits on the internal transfer that funded certificate 2270, and internal transfers never count -> bank_error refund of the full 15.00. Then the assessment rule: counted = 7 > free 6 -> one withdrawal beyond the allowance; the refunded fee covers nothing but still uses one place under the maximum of 6 -> one fee owed, on the seventh counted withdrawal in posting order (the 09-09 overdraft transfer) -> 10.00. Then 527.55 + (25.00 - 15.00) = 537.55 on the 22nd from checking 2605. Same objects, order and values as gold; no alternative reading found.

[Most likely mistakes] counting the ATM withdrawal or the internal transfer; forgetting that overdraft transfers count for Statement Savings; assessing before refunding (owed 0); attaching the owed fee to the 09-08 telephone transfer (sixth, within the allowance); refunding only the 5.00 over the tier fee instead of the full 15.00; refunding as courtesy_waiver; computing the amount from overdraft pulls only.

[Revision log] Round 1: first draft. Round 2: the erroneous fee was reseeded at 15.00 (balance 1,598.57) so the scored amount no longer equals the neither-prerequisite value; the replenishment's quantity was renamed "the withdrawal fees the account bears"; the persona gained the courtesy refusal and lost the recheck branch. Round 3: the overdraft cycle is taken from the most recent overdraft transfer whose counterparty is one of the customer's checking accounts (exact id) instead of a first-row lookup; this dossier was rewritten to match. Round 5 (policy_task revision_4 R4-2, R4-3): the assessment's cap overwrite was withdrawn, so every excess fee row posted in the cycle counts toward excess_withdrawal_fee_max_per_cycle exactly as the frozen parameter, the savings_msr_cycle_excess_fees measure and savings_evt_fee_refund state; a bank_error refund now only stops a fee from covering a withdrawal. The assessment and the replenishment now apply only to the current statement cycle and only while every excess-fee refund posted in the cycle refunds a fee of that cycle (and, for the assessment, every excess fee of the cycle sits on a counted withdrawal beyond the allowance or has been refunded), so counting refunds by the cycle in which they posted always agrees with counting them by the fee's cycle; both conditions are read from the cycle day, the frozen date and source_item_id. World values unchanged: refund 15.00, fee 10.00, amount 537.55.


[Revision log, round 6 (audit rework)] Symptoms (policy_task revision_5 R5-2, R5-T1-a, R5-T1-O1): the round-5 scope conditions of the assessment and the replenishment were in the rules but in no compute binding, and the replenishment's compute_basis attributed them to cyc and refunds; the argument proof of the assessed fee still quoted the round-4 placement wording about a standing fee. Changes: both rules now state their applicability conditions as conditions each read from the records (frozen date and statement_cycle_day; the fees' and refunds' source_item_id; posted dates) and not tested by the computed value, in the same way as the conversion's cap; the replenishment's basis for cyc and refunds now quotes only what those bindings implement; the assessment's conditions were tightened so that a bank_error-refunded fee never sits on a counted withdrawal beyond the allowance (which keeps "carries no fee" and the coverage count consistent) and so that the fee's withdrawal is the only counted withdrawal of its day. Every "most recent" lookup (funding transfer, overdraft transfer) now either requires a single row on the latest date or that all rows of that date share one counterparty, so no row order is used. The quotation in evaluation_criteria[9] now reads "that carries no fee"; the edge_load_bearing text names covered instead of standing; the solvability discriminator no longer speaks of a standing fee. World values unchanged: refund 15.00, fee 10.00, amount 537.55.


[Revision log, round 7 (audit rework)] Symptom (policy_task revision_6 R6-2): the round-6 assessment condition that every unrefunded excess fee sits on a counted withdrawal beyond the allowance depended on posting order within a day, which no record holds, and the round-6 same-day guard covered only the withdrawal taking the new fee (two counted withdrawals sharing a day at the allowance boundary made an existing fee's placement undecidable). Change: the same-day guard is replaced by the condition that no two counted withdrawals of the cycle posted on the same day, so the posting order of all counted withdrawals follows from their posted dates alone; the placement condition now reads "beyond the allowance in that posting order", and every applicability condition is decidable from posted_date, channel, source_item_id, the frozen date and statement_cycle_day. In this world the seven counted withdrawals of 2026-09 fall on seven different days, so every condition holds as before; the argument proof of the assessed withdrawal cites that fact. Values unchanged: refund 15.00, fee 10.00, amount 537.55.


[Revision log, round 8 (audit rework)] Symptom (policy_task revision_7 R7-1): the two refund tools and the fee tool dated their rows today, and the refunds took the account's current statement cycle, while base says "Business day the refund posted", "Statement cycle in which the refund posted" and "Business day the fee posted"; with the clock on Saturday 2026-09-19 the refund's cycle was 2026-09 by the tool and 2026-10 by base, which moved voided (10.00 against nothing) and the replenishment's refunds, and a fee written that day belonged to 2026-09 but posted in the 2026-10 window of savings_msr_cycle_excess_fees. Changes: every posting tool now posts on the business day it posts (today on a business day, otherwise the next business day) and returns the posted_date; the refunds' statement_cycle is the cycle that contains that posted date; the funding refund's rule now says the refund posts on the business day it is made and belongs to the cycle containing that date, instead of placing it in the current statement cycle; the assessment applies only when the frozen date is a business day, the fee rows posted within the cycle's dates are exactly the rows belonging to it (so fee_rows is what savings_msr_cycle_excess_fees counts), and every bank_error refund of a fee of the cycle posted in the cycle; the replenishment applies only when no row on the account has a posted_date later than the frozen date. The Saturday construction now fails these conditions, so nothing is reconciled and no amount is computed under these policies, one answer. This world is a Thursday: the refund and the fee post 2026-09-10 in cycle 2026-09 and every condition holds. Values unchanged: refund 15.00 with statement_cycle 2026-09, fee 10.00, amount 537.55.
user_scenario:
You are Rochelle Gaither, a 36-year-old dental hygienist in Greenville, South Carolina, calling on a short break between patients, friendly but a little rushed. Your savings account at Piedmont Crescent Bank backs up your checking, and this month it has been pulled on again and again. You open by saying what you want, in your own words: "I want a monthly automatic transfer from my checking into my savings that puts back what overdraft protection pulled out of my savings this statement period, plus whatever withdrawal fees the savings actually ends up paying for this period." You want it to run on the 22nd of each month, because your pay lands the day before. You do not know the total and you tell the agent you trust them to add it up from the account.

You hand over details only as the agent asks for them. Your mobile number is 8645550126. For verification you give your date of birth, 1989-10-03, the last four of your Social Security number, 3147, and your ZIP code, 29607; your email, rochelle.gaither@outlook.com, you give only if the agent says the other details were not enough. The savings account is the one ending in 3318, and the money should come from your Everyday checking ending in 2605; you mention the checking only when the agent asks which account the transfer should come from. You want to keep overdraft protection exactly as it is, and if the agent asks whether to change or remove it you say no.

If the agent tells you a fee on the savings was charged by mistake and is being given back, you say that is good news. If the agent tells you a fee that should have been charged is being added now, you sigh, say that's fair if those are the rules, and ask them to make sure the monthly amount still covers everything this period. When the agent gives you a tool to set the transfer up yourself, you use it with the amount, the day and the account details the agent reads out, and you read back what it confirms if asked. If the agent offers to waive or refund a fee as a courtesy or a favor, you turn it down politely: you only want what the bank's own rules say, nothing extra. You never suggest any figure or step of your own and you do not question the agent's arithmetic. Once the agent confirms the monthly transfer is set up, you thank them and hang up.

request_binding.action_semantics: An excess fee on an internal transfer, a channel that never counts, was charged contrary to the charter and is owed back regardless of the request; it is a bank_error refund, not a courtesy waiver.

discriminator.business_meaning: excess fee charged on the uncounted certificate-funding transfer

base_preconditions.condition: The fee's fee_code must be one of courtesy_eligible_fee_codes.
The fee must have posted no more than courtesy_refund_window_days calendar days before the courtesy refund is granted.

The customer's count of savings courtesy refunds in the rolling 365 days must be below the tier's courtesy_refund_limit_365d, counted by savings_msr_courtesy_refunds_365d, where each refunded fee counts as one.
The account's status must be active or dormant when a courtesy refund is granted.
A fee can be refunded at most once.

gold_actions.business_effect: A 10.00 excess withdrawal fee posts on 2026-09-10, a business day, in cycle 2026-09 on the 2026-09-09 overdraft transfer, the seventh counted withdrawal of the cycle.

request_binding.action_semantics: A counted withdrawal beyond the free allowance that carries no fee is an excess fee already owed under the charter; it is a fee assessment, not a refund or a service charge.

stage_provenance.fact: The fee becomes owed once the erroneous fee no longer stands, which the step 7 refund establishes; the counted withdrawals are opening records.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 10.00, computed by savings_ext_counted_withdrawal_fee_assessment: counted 7, free 6, one withdrawal beyond the allowance; the one excess fee row of the cycle was refunded as bank_error at step 7, so it covers nothing (covered 0); every fee row still counts toward the maximum of 6, leaving room 5; owed = MN(1, 5) = 1, charged at P('excess_withdrawal_fee') = 10.00. The rule's applicability conditions hold: 2026-09 is the current cycle; 2026-09-10 is a business day, so the step 7 refund and this fee post on the day of the contact; the only excess fee row of the cycle posted 2026-08-28, inside 2026-08-21..2026-09-20, and belongs to 2026-09; the seven counted withdrawals fall on seven different days; the refunded fee sits on the uncounted internal transfer; and the one bank_error refund, posted in 2026-09, refunds that 2026-09 fee.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.statement_cycle: 2026-09. Basis: savings_fee statement_cycle is "Statement cycle the fee belongs to" and the docstring asks for the cycle of the withdrawal; the 2026-09-09 withdrawal carries statement_cycle 2026-09. The fee itself posts 2026-09-10 (a Thursday, a business day), inside that cycle, so it is also one of the rows savings_msr_cycle_excess_fees counts for 2026-09.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The order is pinned, not free: the assessment policy states that every erroneous excess fee of the cycle must already have been refunded before the fees owed are counted (its voided count reads the refund), and the replenishment policy counts the fees the account bears only after every refund and every owed fee has posted. Refund, then assessment, then the automatic transfer is the only topological order; an assessment computed before the refund finds owed = 0, and the root would then read 527.55 + 15.00 = 542.55.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Replaying gold without the step 9 fee gives fees the account bears 15.00 - 15.00 = 0.00 and automatic_transfer_amount 527.55 instead of 537.55; the terminal state also lacks the 10.00 fee on the 2026-09-09 overdraft transfer and the balance ends 1,613.57 instead of 1,603.57.

Replaying gold without the step 7 refund (step 9 fee kept) gives fees the account bears 25.00 and automatic_transfer_amount 552.55 instead of 537.55; the terminal state lacks the bank_error refund row and the balance ends 1,588.57. Skipping both prerequisites gives 527.55 + 15.00 = 542.55, also different from gold.

Without the step 7 refund the assessment computes voided 0, covered 1, owed 0 and result 0.00 instead of 10.00, so no fee would be charged on the seventh counted withdrawal (verified by check_compute value_input replay); the policy's own condition (an unrefunded fee sits on an uncounted withdrawal) also fails.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only for a monthly transfer that puts back what overdraft protection took this statement period plus the withdrawal fees the savings actually ends up paying. It never mentions the certificate-funding fee, a missing fee, a refund, the free-withdrawal count or any correction; any reaction about fees is passive, after the agent reports them.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: set_savings_automatic_transfer_e1e909eb only writes the amount, day and funding account; assess_savings_withdrawal_fee_aafc1fb2 and refund_savings_withdrawal_fee_774e6cc0 only post a row and adjust the balance. None reads the ledger to check fees, counts or refunds, none refuses, errors or hints.

od_d = LATEST posted_date of overdraft_transfer withdrawals = 2026-09-09; od_cp = counterparty of the overdraft transfer of that date = checking account ending 2605; od_same = True (the only overdraft transfer that day); od_chk = CFIELD('checking','checking_account_id', checking_account_id=od_cp) = that account, one of the customer's checking accounts [history + cross-category read, exact id].
cyc = statement_cycle of that latest overdraft transfer = 2026-09, the current statement cycle (cycle day 20, frozen 2026-09-10), so the cycle is within this policy [history].

chans = [online_transfer, mobile_app_transfer, telephone_banking, ach_debit, wire_domestic] (Statement Savings): n_online 1 (08-21), n_mobile 0, n_phone 1 (09-08), n_ach 0, n_check 0 (money_market_check not listed: untriggered branch), n_wire 0 [history + tier].

n_od = 5 overdraft transfers (08-24, 08-27, 08-31, 09-03, 09-09) counted by channel because overdraft_transfer_counts_toward_limit is true; ATM 08-25 and the certificate-funding internal transfer 08-28 never count.
counted = 7; free = P('free_withdrawals_per_cycle') = 6; beyond = MX(7 - 6, 0) = 1 counted withdrawal beyond the allowance.

fee_rows = 1 excess fee row posted in 2026-09 (the erroneous 15.00 fee); voided = 1 bank_error excess refund posted in 2026-09 (step 7), and it refunds a fee of 2026-09; covered = 1 - 1 = 0; room = MX(6 - 1, 0) = 5 under the per-cycle maximum, counting every fee row as savings_msr_cycle_excess_fees does [history at handling time].
owed = MX(MN(1 - 0, 5), 0) = 1; result = RND(P('excess_withdrawal_fee') = 10.00) = 10.00. Without the step 7 refund, voided = 0, covered = 1, owed = 0 and the result would be 0.

od_d / od_cp / od_same / od_chk as in the assessment: the overdraft transfer of 2026-09-09 is the only one that day and its counterparty is the customer's Everyday Checking ending 2605 [cross-category read, exact id]; cyc = 2026-09, which is also the current statement cycle, so the policy applies.
od_total = every overdraft transfer of 2026-09 = 120.00 + 85.50 + 64.25 + 210.00 + 47.80 = 527.55 (all five went to checking 2605) [history].
fees = excess_withdrawal fee amounts of 2026-09 at handling time = 15.00 (erroneous, 08-28) + 10.00 (assessed at step 9) = 25.00 [history after prior gold writes].
refunds = excess_withdrawal refunds posted in 2026-09 = 15.00 (step 7); fees_net = MX(25.00 - 15.00, 0) = 10.00.
need = 527.55 + 10.00 = 537.55; floor = P('automatic_transfer_min_amount') = 25.00; need < floor is false (untriggered).

result = RND(537.55) = 537.55. On the opening world (neither prerequisite resolved) the same formula gives 527.55 + 15.00 = 542.55; without step 9 it gives 527.55; without step 7 (step 9 fee kept) 552.55. The rule's applicability conditions hold: 2026-09 is the current cycle, no row on the account has a posted_date after 2026-09-10 (the refund and the fee posted that business day), and the one excess-fee refund posted in 2026-09 refunds a 2026-09 fee.
